title: Triangles and Quadrilaterals by Angles Assessment
description: Checkpoint on constructing and judging triangles and quadrilaterals from angle conditions.

questions.question: Which angle set can form a triangle?
questions.explanation: 50 + 60 + 70 = 180, so this set can form a triangle.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 42 degrees, 68 degrees, and x. What is x? Enter just the number.
A triangle can have two angles that measure 100 degrees each.
questions.explanation: 100 + 100 = 200, which already exceeds the triangle angle sum of 180.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has angles 85 degrees, 95 degrees, 110 degrees, and x. What is x?
Which angle set can form a quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: 75 + 85 + 95 + 105 = 360, so this set can form a quadrilateral.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has three angles measuring 100 degrees, 100 degrees, and 80 degrees. What is the fourth angle? Enter just the number.
A quadrilateral with angles 150 degrees, 90 degrees, 70 degrees, and 50 degrees is possible.
questions.explanation: 150 + 90 + 70 + 50 = 360, so the angle sum fits a quadrilateral.

questions.question: Why is a triangle with angles 0 degrees, 80 degrees, and 100 degrees impossible?
options: A triangle cannot have a 0-degree interior angle
A triangle cannot have an obtuse angle
The angles must all be equal
questions.explanation: Even though 0 + 80 + 100 = 180, an interior angle must be greater than 0 degrees.

questions.question: A student wants to draw a quadrilateral with angles 100 degrees, 120 degrees, 80 degrees, and 70 degrees. Explain whether the construction is possible.
questions.correctAnswer: It is impossible because 100 + 120 + 80 + 70 = 370, but quadrilateral angles must add to 360 degrees.
questions.explanation: The explanation should add the angles and compare the result with 360 degrees.

questions.question: Describe the first two checks you should make before drawing a figure from given angle conditions.
questions.correctAnswer: First identify whether the figure is a triangle or quadrilateral. Then check whether the angles add to 180 degrees for a triangle or 360 degrees for a quadrilateral.
questions.explanation: A good construction plan starts by choosing the correct angle-sum rule and checking that the conditions fit it.
